title: Resistance and Survival
subtitle: The kingdoms and communities that refused to disappear

hero.title: RESISTANCE & SURVIVAL
hero.subtitle: The Civilisation That Refused to Disappear
hero.summary: The history of medieval Bharat is not only a history of conquest. It is also a history of resistance, adaptation, political recovery and cultural survival.

abstract: Conquest never erased the civilisation of Bharat. Rajput kingdoms, southern powers, the Ahoms, Vijayanagara and later the Marathas demonstrate different forms of military and political resistance.

sections.title: RESISTANCE BEGAN AT THE FRONTIER
content: The Hindu Shahi rulers and later frontier powers fought repeatedly to contain Ghaznavid expansion. Their defeats were severe, but they demonstrate that invasion was contested rather than passively accepted.

sections.title: RAJPUT RESISTANCE
content: Rajput polities repeatedly contested the expansion of the Delhi Sultanate. Their political fragmentation was a weakness, but their military culture also generated sustained resistance across Rajasthan and neighbouring regions.
Prithviraj Chauhan became the most famous literary symbol of this resistance, especially through the *Prithviraj Raso* tradition.

sections.title: VIJAYANAGARA
content: The Vijayanagara Empire became one of the most important political powers of southern India. Its rulers presented themselves as protectors of dharma and built a powerful state centred on military organisation, temple patronage and economic networks.
Its history demonstrates that the medieval period cannot be reduced to a single north Indian narrative.

sections.title: THE AHOMS
content: In the north-east, the Ahom kingdom developed a durable political and military system and resisted Mughal expansion for generations.
Their history is a powerful reminder that regional state formation and geography could produce very different outcomes from those in the Gangetic plain.

sections.title: THE MARATHA ASCENDANCY
content: The rise of the Marathas created another major centre of political resistance and eventually challenged Mughal power on a subcontinental scale.
The story of Shivaji and the Maratha state belongs to the longer history of political recovery and the reassertion of indigenous power.

sections.title: SURVIVAL IS ALSO VICTORY
content: The civilisation of Bharat survived conquest because communities rebuilt institutions, preserved languages and texts, maintained pilgrimage networks, protected temples, created new states and transmitted cultural memory.
The historical lesson is not that Bharat was never defeated. It is that defeat did not become disappearance.

researchQuestions: How did different Indian states adapt their military systems?
What institutions enabled cultural continuity under political domination?
How did temple patronage and pilgrimage networks preserve identity?
